name: Pittidae
description: Pittas are colorful, ground-dwelling passerines with stout legs and short tails. They are found primarily in tropical Asia and Australasia, with one species in Africa.

children.name: Hydrornis
children.description: A genus of medium-sized to large pittas found in tropical Asia, characterised by more subdued plumage than the typical pittas, often with intricate barred or banded patterns. They are secretive, ground-dwelling birds of forest understorey.

children.name: Hydrornis soror
children.description: The blue-rumped pitta (Hydrornis soror) is a species of bird in the family Pittidae. It is found in Cambodia, China, Laos, Thailand, and Vietnam. Its natural habitats are subtropical or tropical seasonal forest and subtropical or tropical moist montane forest.

children.name: Hydrornis oatesi
children.description: The rusty-naped pitta (Hydrornis oatesi) is a species of bird in the family Pittidae.

children.name: Hydrornis cyaneus
children.description: The blue pitta (Hydrornis cyaneus) is a species of bird in the family Pittidae found in the northeastern Indian subcontinent, southern China, and Indochina. It typically lives in moist forests but can also inhabit dry forest. It is an unobtrusive, solitary bird which feeds by foraging on the ground for insects and other small invertebrates.

children.name: Hydrornis irena
children.description: The Malayan banded pitta (Hydrornis irena) is a species of bird in the family Pittidae. Other common names include the blue-tailed pitta, the Irene's pitta, the banded pitta and the Van den Bosch's pitta. It is found in Thailand, the Malay Peninsula and Sumatra. It was formerly considered conspecific with the Bornean and Javan banded pittas, together they were referred to as the banded pitta, but now they are considered to be separate species.

children.name: Hydrornis guajanus
children.description: The Javan banded pitta (Hydrornis guajanus) is a species of bird in the family Pittidae. It is found in Java and Bali. It was formerly considered conspecific with the Bornean and Malayan banded pittas. Together, they were referenced as the banded pitta.

children.name: Hydrornis caerulea
children.description: A very large pitta with blue upperparts, found in the lowland forests of Southeast Asia.

children.name: Hydrornis baudii
children.description: The blue-headed pitta (Hydrornis baudii) is a species of bird in the pitta family Pittidae. It is endemic to Borneo.

children.name: Hydrornis nipalensis
children.description: The blue-naped pitta (Hydrornis nipalensis) is a species of bird in the family Pittidae.

children.name: Pitta
children.description: Pitta is the largest genus of pittas, containing most of the family's species across tropical Asia, Australasia, and Africa.

children.name: Pitta anerythra
children.description: The black-faced pitta (Pitta anerythra) is a species of bird in the family Pittidae. It is found on Bougainville Island in Papua New Guinea (subspecies pallida), and Choiseul Island (subspecies nigrifrons) as well as Santa Isabel Island (nominate form) in the Solomon Islands. Its natural habitat is subtropical or tropical moist lowland forest. It is threatened by habitat loss and most certainly by introduced predators and/or competitors.

children.name: Pitta erythrogaster

children.name: Pitta gurneyi
children.description: Gurney's pitta (Hydrornis gurneyi) is a medium-sized passerine bird. It breeds in the Malay Peninsula, with populations mainly in Myanmar. The common name and Latin binomial commemorate the British banker and amateur ornithologist John Henry Gurney (1819-1890). Its diet consists of slugs, insects, and earthworms.

children.name: Pitta iris
children.description: The rainbow pitta (Pitta iris) is a small passerine bird in the pitta family, Pittidae, endemic to northern Australia, most closely related to the superb pitta of Manus Island.

children.name: Pitta kochi
children.description: The whiskered pitta (Erythropitta kochi) is a species of bird in the family Pittidae.

children.name: Pitta maxima
children.description: The ivory-breasted pitta (Pitta maxima) is a species of bird in the family Pittidae. It is endemic to North Maluku in Indonesia, known as Paok halmahera. Its natural habitat is subtropical or tropical moist lowland forests.

children.name: Pitta megarhyncha
children.description: The mangrove pitta (Pitta megarhyncha) is a species of passerine bird in the family Pittidae native to the eastern Indian subcontinent and western Southeast Asia.

children.name: Pitta moluccensis
children.description: The blue-winged pitta (Pitta moluccensis) is a passerine bird in the family Pittidae. It forms a superspecies with three other pittas, the Indian pitta (P. Brachyura), the fairy pitta (P. Nympha) and the mangrove pitta (P. Megarhyncha). A colourful bird, it has a black head with a buff stripe above the eye, a white collar, greenish upper parts, blue wings, buff underparts and a reddish vent area. Its range extends from India to Malaysia, Indonesia, southern China and the Philippines. Its habitat is moist woodland, parks and gardens and it avoids dense forest. It feeds mainly on insects and worms. It breeds in the spring, building an untidy spherical nest on the ground, often near water and between tree roots. A clutch of about five eggs is laid and incubated by both parents, hatching after about sixteen days.

children.name: Pitta nigritifrons

children.name: Pitta phayrei

children.name: Pitta reichenowi
children.description: The green-breasted pitta (Pitta reichenowi) is a species of bird in the family Pittidae. It is one of only two Pitta species in Africa, and is found in deep forest of the tropics.

children.name: Pitta schneideri
children.description: Schneider's pitta (Hydrornis schneideri) is a species of bird in the family Pittidae. It is endemic to Sumatra in Indonesia. Its natural habitat is subtropical or tropical moist montane forest. It is threatened by habitat loss. It was rediscovered in 1988 after last being seen in 1918.

children.name: Pitta sordida
children.description: The western hooded pitta is a passerine bird in the family Pittidae. It is common in eastern and southeastern Asia and maritime Southeast Asia, where it lives in several types of forests as well as on plantations and other cultivated areas. It is a green bird with a black head and chestnut crown.

children.name: Pitta soror
children.description: The blue-rumped pitta (Hydrornis soror) is a species of bird in the family Pittidae. It is found in Cambodia, China, Laos, Thailand, and Vietnam. Its natural habitats are subtropical or tropical seasonal forest and subtropical or tropical moist montane forest.

children.name: Pitta steerii
children.description: The azure-breasted pitta (Pitta steerii) is a species of bird in the family Pittidae. It is a striking and colorful bird having colors of red, azure, green, black and white, It is endemic to the islands of Mindanao, Bohol, Leyte and Samar in the Philippines. Along with the Whiskered pitta, it is one of two endemic pittas in the country. Its natural habitat is tropical moist lowland forest. It is threatened by habitat loss.

children.name: Pitta superba
children.description: The superb pitta (Pitta superba) is a large pitta that is endemic to Manus Island which lies to the north of Papua New Guinea.

children.name: Pitta venusta
children.description: The graceful pitta (Erythropitta venusta), sometimes alternatively known as the black-crowned pitta (although this term is more regularly applied to Erythropitta ussheri), is a species of bird in the family Pittidae.

children.name: Pitta versicolor
children.description: The noisy pitta (Pitta versicolor) is a species of bird in the family Pittidae.

children.name: Pitta vigorsii
children.description: The Banda Sea pitta or two-striped pitta (Pitta vigorsii) is a species of bird in the family Pittidae. It is found in Indonesia. Its natural habitat is subtropical or tropical moist lowland forest. It is threatened by habitat loss.
